title: How the Python SDK names ZCC keys on the wire: the model serializer and the parameter mapper

prose.text: ZCC keys mix camelCase, snake_case and odd acronyms, and they differ by platform block, so the Python SDK carries its own key handling for ZCC bodies and query parameters. The general rule is [[zcc.api.conventions:python-body-casing]]; this subject holds how the serializer decides and where it falls short.

serializer-scope.statement: The ZCC serializer takes the model class as the single source of truth for wire keys, applies to ZCC only, and passes unknown keys through rather than dropping them.

quotes: The model class is the single source of truth for wire keys.
This module applies to ZCC only and must not be used by other services.
camelCase wire keys passed by the user are accepted as-is; unknown keys
pass through unchanged so we never silently drop or mangle data.

resolution-order.statement: Each key is resolved in order: a snake_case attribute the model declares takes the model's wire key; a key that is already one of the model's wire keys is kept; a key in `WebPolicy.SNAKE_CASE_KEYS` stays snake_case; anything else is camel-cased by the generic helper, which leaves a key without an underscore unchanged.

quotes: 3. Snake_case key listed in the legacy ``WebPolicy.SNAKE_CASE_KEYS`` set -> preserve as snake_case.
Already-camelCase keys pass through unchanged because the converter is a no-op for strings without an underscore.

field-map-traced.statement: The attribute-to-wire-key map is found by running the model's `request_format` against a tracing object, so only entries whose value is a direct `self.<attr>` reference are mapped; literal or computed values are skipped.

nested-fallback.statement: A nested dict or list whose key the model ties to a nested model class is serialized against that class; one with no declared class goes through the older selective camel-case converter instead.

serializer-callers.statement: Two ZCC writes use the serializer: `web_policy_edit` with the `WebPolicy` model and `update_forwarding_profile` with the `ForwardingProfile` model. `zcc_to_wire` returns a `_ZccWireBody`. When the endpoint contains `/zcc/` (both modules' base endpoint is `/zcc/papi/public/v1`), the executor returns such a body as a plain dict with no key conversion, and any other non-empty dict body gets the selective camel-case conversion.
serializer-callers.conditions: Searching zscaler/zcc for `zcc_to_wire(` finds only these two calls. Narrowed to the OneAPI client: the legacy client strips `/zcc` from the path first, so this branch does not match there (legacy-client-full-camel-case).

legacy-client-full-camel-case.statement: On the legacy ZCC client, every ZCC body, a serialized `_ZccWireBody` included, is camel-cased in full by the generic helper, where only FIELD_EXCEPTIONS entries such as `exit_password` stay as mapped, so snake_case wire keys such as top-level `device_type` and `pac_url` and the Windows `disable_password` and `install_ssl_certs` go out camelCase.
legacy-client-full-camel-case.conditions: Traced: the legacy executor has `use_legacy_client` true via `zcc_legacy_client`, so `create_request` strips the `/zcc` prefix before `_prepare_body`, and the `"/zcc/" in endpoint` branch never matches; not sent.

numeric-strings-rejected.statement: For `os_type`, the mapper keeps a string only when its lower-cased form is a platform name in its map, and raises ValueError when nothing is kept; for `device_type`, it keeps such names and integers (`isinstance(dt, int)`), and raises ValueError likewise. A numeric string such as "3" is neither, so it raises ValueError, although the `list_devices` and `activate_web_policy` docstring examples pass "3" and '3'.

mapper-keyword-only.statement: The mapper reads `query_params` only from keyword arguments, so a dict passed positionally is not mapped: its `os_type` name goes out camel-cased as `osType=windows`.
